rationale: Greek προσχαρίζομαι (πρός 'in addition' + χαρίζομαι 'grant freely'). Coordinated with simple ⲭⲁⲣⲓⲍⲉ (line 18) in a προσ-/simple contrast: the gods grant the petitioner's own request (χαρίζομαι); when one prays for another, they grant 'in addition' the request for the other (προσχαρίζομαι). The προσ- preserves the supererogatory force essential to the chapter's theology of intercessory prayer.

Lycopolitan ⲥⲉⲝⲉ = Sahidic ϣⲁϫⲉ 'word, saying, matter' (cf. accumulated ⲥⲉⲭⲉ which gives same root). Variant orthography ⲝ vs. ⲭ for Sahidic ϫ. Functions throughout this page (lines 2, 11) as the topic-noun for the disciple's question.

Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' with -ϩ object suffix (= -ϥ). The form ⲡⲁⲝⲉϩ ⲁⲣⲁϩ (line 1) doubles the dative — 'he-said-to-him to him' — standard Coptic redundancy. Cf. accumulated ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ, ⲡⲁⲭⲉ, ⲡⲁⲭⲉϩ same root with orthographic variation.

Lycopolitan qualitative form, tentatively from ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'proclaim, send forth' = Sahidic ⲧⲁⲩⲏⲩ. Used here of the matter 'proclaimed before men.' Alternative reading: qualitative of ⲁⲓⲁⲓ 'multiply' = 'has multiplied/grown great.' Confidence moderate; either reading fits the discourse.
Lycopolitan variant of ϣⲗⲏⲛ/ϣⲗⲏⲗ 'pray, prayer' with ⲛ for ⲗ — confirmed by the parallel use of ϣⲗⲏⲛ in lines 3, 23. Both forms appear in this kephalaion as the standard term for prayer.

Plural substantival of ⲍⲟⲩⲓⲧ 'foremost' (in glossary as ⲡⲍⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲧ 'the foremost/chief'). Used here cosmologically: 'this prayer came into being from the firsts' = from the primordial cosmic beings. Recurs in line 26 ⲛⲓϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲉⲧⲟ ⲛϣⲁⲣⲡ 'the firsts that are foremost' parallel construction.

Verbal idiom ⲣ̄- + ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ ('first') + ⲛ̄- (linking) + ⲧⲱⲃⲍ ('pray') = 'do-first the praying' = 'pray first/foremost.' Standard Coptic 'do-first the action' construction with Lycopolitan dialect features. Names the cosmogonic precedence of divine prayer.

Relative ⲧⲉⲧ- + Greek φορεῖ 'wears/bears.' Fixed Manichaean ecclesiological epithet for the earthly Holy Church distinguishing her from the cosmic divine assemblies. The flesh-bearing Church participates in prayer alongside the gods' prayer.
